info.title: Planir Orchestrator API
info.description: Generic, client-agnostic runtime provider over hardened sandboxed compute. A runtime is a durable, client-owned handle to a single sandboxed workload with its own persistent volume. Lifecycle verbs are async + idempotent (flip desired state → 202; the change applies shortly). The API exposes no placement detail beyond the region you choose, no direct network address for a workload, no storage backend, and no caller-domain concept — `clientRef` is the only correlation handle, and it is opaque. Rate limits: every /v1 route is metered per API key — a token bucket at the key's sustained rate (default 10 req/s) with a 2× burst, raised by a package override. Over budget → 429 `RATE_LIMITED` with a `Retry-After` header (whole seconds until a token refills); each route documents the 429. A 429 without a `Retry-After` header comes from infrastructure in front of the platform — treat it as retry-with-backoff regardless of body.

servers.description: The published contract URL — also every generated client's default baseUrl.

tags.name: runtimes
tags.description: Runtime lifecycle, config, reach, logs, usage, events.

serviceToken.description: Scoped service token bound to a caller principal. Missing/invalid → 401 UNAUTHENTICATED.

Error.description: The error envelope. `code` is an OPEN enum: new codes are additive under the platform compatibility policy — clients MUST tolerate codes not in this list (treat an unknown code as an unretryable failure of the request). Per-operation responses reference named schemas that narrow `code` to exactly what that operation+status emits; the wire shape is identical everywhere.

id.description: The event id (`evt_<n>`, monotonic) — identical to the `webhook-id` header, and STABLE across retries and manual redelivery: deduplicate by it.

version.description: Envelope version. New event types arrive additively and never change it.

timestamp.description: When the event occurred (not when this delivery was attempted).

team_id.description: The team the runtime belongs to.

region.description: The public location of the runtime the event concerns — the same `region` its API responses echo (read at delivery time). No narrower placement detail ever appears.

WebhookEventType.description: A lifecycle event type, dot-namespaced. `created` = the runtime record exists; `running` = observed running; `error` = observed in error (fires per transition — deduplicate by event id); `destroyed` = observed destroyed (terminal). New types arrive additively; unknown types in a filter are refused at registration.

UnauthenticatedError.description: The request carries no credential, or one that does not resolve to a live key.

TeamBlockedError.description: The team is blocked: writes and non-billing reads are refused until support unblocks it.

RateLimitedError.description: The per-key request-rate budget is exhausted; wait `Retry-After` seconds and retry.

memoryBytes.description: Customer workload container hard memory limit in bytes. Minimum 134217728 (128 MiB) — below that no real image starts, so sub-floor requests are rejected here instead of surfacing as a confusing workload failure after boot.

cpuMillis.description: Customer workload container CPU quota in millicores (1000 = 1 vCPU of quota).

storageBytes.description: Persistent volume size in bytes. The volume is mounted read-write at `/data` inside the workload; it survives stop/start and follows the runtime for life. Durability: every live volume is backed up daily to off-site object storage — 7-day retention. Backups are crash-consistent disaster-recovery copies: a restore point is normally under 24 hours old and never silently older than 26 hours — past that the platform raises an alarm. Keep your own backups of critical data. A live volume restore is on request today and arrives as a NEW volume (self-serve restore is planned). Volumes are not live-replicated. Writable by the workload's own user, whatever the image runs as — root or not, no setup needed: the volume root arrives group-writable to a platform group the workload process automatically carries as a supplementary group. Files the workload creates keep their normal ownership. Software that demands strict permissions on its data directory (e.g. PostgreSQL's initdb) should use a subdirectory and set its own mode (`mkdir -m 700 /data/pgdata`). This is the only metered disk.

ephemeralStorageBytes.description: Rootfs scratch-disk budget in bytes. The rootfs is a real block disk of a fixed tier size (4 or 8 GiB); the ask rounds UP to the smallest tier that fits, and `df /` inside the workload reports that tier honestly. Persistence follows `preserveRootfs` (default true): `stop` commits the disk and the next `start` resumes it. Any OTHER restart — a crash, or a config/env change that recreates the workload — begins from the last committed image (the original image if it has never been stopped), so writes since that boot are lost. Durable data belongs on `/data`, which is unaffected either way. Bundled, never billed. Omitted → 4 GiB default. Free up to the 8 GiB cap; above the cap the request is rejected 422 — contact sales. Reads echo the requested value, never null. Filling the disk gives the writing process a plain ENOSPC write error — the workload keeps running; deleting files frees space immediately.

port.description: Container port the HTTP readiness check hits.

httpPath.description: HTTP path probed for readiness; 2xx/3xx = ready.

ReadinessSpec.description: The explicit readiness gate as set at create. Absent = the TCP-first-port default.

allowOut.description: Allowlist mode when present: ONLY these destinations are reachable. Entries: IPv4 CIDRs or domain patterns (`*.` prefix wildcard). Domain rules follow DNS resolution — the documented industry limitation.

denyOut.description: Destinations denied even when allowed (deny wins). IPv4 CIDRs ONLY — no platform on this substrate class denies by domain; use allowOut to constrain by domain. Alone (no allowOut): open egress minus these ranges.

NetworkSpec.description: The egress posture currently applied. Absent = the open default.

phase.description: Observed box lifecycle phase. `running` means the Planir agent container is running; a port-bearing runtime additionally requires current Reach endpoint confirmation. Application readiness and entrypoint state do not otherwise govern this field. A runtime that stays `provisioning` for 5 minutes (300 000 ms) without reaching box-running flips to `error` — image-pull, box-boot, and agent crash-loop failures surface this way. `error` is not terminal: the platform keeps retrying, and a box that later runs returns to `running`. `unschedulable` means the location is waiting on capacity for this runtime — distinct from `provisioning` (coming up) and `error` (crashed/stuck), exempt from the 5-minute deadline, and self-correcting: when capacity frees it converges to `running` with no client action. Compute bills zero in the span; destroying instead of waiting is the client's call. `stopping` covers the whole stop teardown — from the stop being acted on until the compute is fully released (`stopped`); compute bills until the scheduled allocation is released. The set is additive over time — treat unknown phases as not-yet-running.

generation.description: The desired generation this reflects. 0 means no desired generation has been acknowledged.

restarts.description: Planir agent container restart count. Absent until compute has been observed. A climbing count while phase sits at `provisioning` means the box supervisor is crashing at boot.

reason.description: Coarse terminal label (`Error`, `OOMKilled`, …) — stable vocabulary, not prose.

at.description: When the container last exited (ISO-8601), if known.

lastExit.description: The Planir agent container's last terminal exit. Absent while it has never died. Customer entrypoint state is reported separately in `observed.entrypoint`.

entrypoint.description: Current customer entrypoint state from the in-box agent. Signal exits use `128 + signal`. Absent unless the box is running and current agent status was observed; last-only, with no exit history.

waitingReason.description: Present exactly while the workload is stuck waiting on its IMAGE — a stable, machine-readable value, never raw registry text. A private image missing/mismatching its registry credential surfaces here as `ErrImagePull`/`ImagePullBackOff` long before the 5-minute `error` flip. A stored credential change becomes available after asynchronous propagation; a later pull can then recover without another lifecycle verb. Absent = not waiting on an image (normal boot, running, crashed — see `phase`/`lastExit` for those). The set is additive over time.

Observed.description: Absent until the platform records its first observation — normally within a few seconds of create. Absence means "not yet observed", never an error.

timeout.description: Configured runtime lifetime in seconds. 0 means unlimited.

timeoutAt.description: Current absolute deadline while a configured runtime is desired-running; null otherwise.

onTimeout.description: Configured deadline action. Present only while timeout is positive.

generation.description: Starts at 1. Increments for a real start, stop, destroy, timeout lifecycle action, config change, effective environment change, runtime-key rotation, network change, restart, or first accepted force termination. Canonically identical replays and metadata, timeout-policy, registry-credential, agent-token, and provider-state updates do not increment it.

spawn.description: Whether runtime-bound child management is enabled.

image.description: The image ref this runtime runs (echoed from create).

env.description: The env map, echoed in full ({} when none) — env is configuration, not a secret store.

command.description: The CMD override as set at create. Absent = the resolved image CMD was used. This field echoes the request override, not the resolved final argv.

entrypoint.description: The ENTRYPOINT override as set at create. Absent = the resolved image ENTRYPOINT was used. This field echoes the request override, not the resolved final argv.

rootfsReadOnly.description: The rootfs hardening knob as set at create (default false).

preserveRootfs.description: Rootfs preservation at stop as set at create (default true) — false = the throwaway stop (rootfs discarded, `/data` survives).

items.description: Internal port the workload listens on (HTTP). Declared by the client; never inferred.

ports.description: Exposed ports the client declared at create (echoed back as bare integers).

urls.description: Reach handle per declared port, keyed by the port number as a string ({} when no ports are declared). The same opaque, placement-free handle POST /v1/runtimes/{id}/reach returns — the client parses nothing out of it. The handle exists from create; it serves traffic once the workload passes readiness (before that the edge answers with an error status).

metadata.description: Correlation labels, echoed in full ({} when none).

region.description: The public location this runtime runs in (e.g. "brq") — the resolved value, always present (the client's choice, or the default when omitted). No narrower placement detail is exposed.

InvalidRequestError.description: Shape validation refused the request: bad JSON, a malformed field, or a violated bound.

InsufficientBalanceError.description: Metered admission refused the create/start: the balance is not positive. Top up first.

RuntimeCreateNotFoundError.description: The volume is unavailable, or the image is absent or inaccessible; code distinguishes the resource class.

RuntimeCreateConflictError.description: Create refused by a conflict — `code` names which. CONFLICT: the Idempotency-Key was reused with a DIFFERENT effective request (same key + same request replays idempotently; a different request needs a fresh key). VOLUME_BUSY: the volume named by `volumeId` is attached elsewhere — destroy the holding runtime first. INVALID_STATE: the volume is still creating; retry when it is available.

RuntimeCreatePolicyError.description: A create policy or permanent image-input condition refused the request; code names the cause.

LimitExceededError.description: A limit refused the request — `code` names which: RATE_LIMITED = request-rate budget (wait `Retry-After`, retry); CONCURRENCY_LIMIT = the running-runtime cap (a quota — destroy a runtime or raise the cap; retrying without that cannot succeed, and no Retry-After is sent); RESOURCE_QUOTA = a per-family vCPU/memory ceiling would be passed (resource-governance Gate C) or the team's total provisioned-storage entitlement would be passed; release the named resource or raise its entitlement (no Retry-After).

ProvisioningUnavailableError.description: New allocation is temporarily unavailable because placement has no capacity, billing catch-up is incomplete, or the image registry is unavailable. Nothing is provisioned or charged; retry later.

clientRef.description: Opaque client correlation handle. No shared id-space, no FK. Optional — the orchestrator generates one when omitted (echoed on reads).

image.description: Resolved container image ref the orchestrator pulls. Echoed back on every Runtime read. Private images are supported via stored registry credentials (`/v1/registry-credentials`), matched by registry host with no extra create field. Compatible examples are GHCR PAT, GitLab deploy token, quay robot, GAR `_json_key`, and ACR service principal; ECR is unsupported because its 12-hour tokens are not long-lived static credentials. Fresh create uses the current committed credential when it contacts the host origin. Later origin pulls observe credential changes after asynchronous propagation; the prior state can remain effective until then. A rejected effective credential is not retried anonymously at that origin. Running containers continue through credential changes. The image is resolved to a digest at create; the digest fixes the later image identity, but create-time process metadata is not bound to those bytes. Images that require their own PID 1, such as systemd or s6 images, are unsupported. Images that require content at /__planir or /__planir-state are unsupported.

config.description: Optional opaque workload config, base64 over the wire (see the config description). Omitted = no config file is mounted at /etc/planir/config.

env.description: Optional env vars (default {}). See the EnvMap description.

spawn.description: Issue one runtime-bound credential for depth-one child runtime management.

command.description: Optional CMD override (argv array, no shell). With no entrypoint override, it replaces the image CMD and follows the image ENTRYPOINT. Omitted = image CMD. Create-time only — there is no replace verb; recreate to change it.

entrypoint.description: Optional ENTRYPOINT override (argv array, no shell). It replaces the image ENTRYPOINT and image CMD; an explicit command is appended. Omitted = image ENTRYPOINT. Create-time only — there is no replace verb.

volumeId.description: Attach an EXISTING standalone volume (POST /v1/volumes) at `/data` instead of auto-creating one. The volume defines the storage size — mutually exclusive with `resources.storageBytes` (400 when both are present); mount and ownership semantics are identical. Runtime destroy then DETACHES the volume (back to `available`, data intact) instead of deleting it. The volume must be `available`: still creating → 409 INVALID_STATE; attached elsewhere → 409 VOLUME_BUSY; unknown, another team's id, or deletion accepted → 404. Omitted = an auto-created volume that is deleted with the runtime (the default lifecycle).

items.description: Internal port the workload listens on (HTTP). Declared by the client; never inferred.

ports.description: Exposed ports the orchestrator routes the public handle to, as bare integers (e.g. [8080]). Omitted or [] = no public surface; never inferred from the image. Port numbers must be unique.

allOf.description: Optional explicit HTTP readiness gate for public reach. The path must answer before reach is published. Omitted = a TCP probe on the FIRST declared port; with no declared ports there is no application probe or public reach. Readiness does not govern `observed.phase`. Exactly ONE probe ever. Create-time only.
Optional egress posture (see NetworkSpec). Omitted = open egress minus the standing SSRF/private deny. Replaceable later via PUT /network (applies live, no restart).

metadata.description: Optional correlation labels (default {}). See the metadata description.

rootfsReadOnly.description: Hardening knob, default false. false (default): the rootfs is writable — a standard machine; writes land in the ephemeral scratch budget. true: the rootfs is the image verbatim, read-only, with writable /tmp and /run scratch mounts (funded by the same budget); anything durable belongs on `/data`.

preserveRootfs.description: Rootfs preservation at stop, default true. true (default): `stop` commits the full rootfs to an image and the next `start` continues from it — everything the workload wrote (installed tools, cloned repos, system config) survives, held in durable storage while parked. false: the throwaway stop — the rootfs is discarded and `start` boots the original image (writes gone), `/data` intact. Create-time only — there is no per-stop override.

timeout.description: Runtime lifetime in seconds. Omitted or 0 = unlimited. A positive value arms the deadline while desiredState is running.

onTimeout.description: Action at the configured positive timeout. Omitted with a positive timeout = stop.

desiredState.description: Initial desired state (default running). Cannot create destroyed.

region.description: Optional location to run in — the public region label (e.g. "brq"), a plain string, NEVER an enum. Discover the offered values via GET /v1/regions. Omitted = the cheapest available location for the chosen preset. A location that exists but does not offer this preset's family → 422; a location that is full or not yet live → 503 NO_CAPACITY. Never a silent cross-location fallback. Echoed on every read.

ResourceSpecInput.description: Optional resource allocation. Omitted = the published defaults: workload CPU quota cpuMillis 1000, workload memory limit memoryBytes 2147483648 (2 GiB), and storageBytes 4294967296 (4 GiB). Reads always echo the effective values.

nextCursor.description: Pass verbatim as `?cursor=` for the next page. Absent = this is the last page.

RuntimeNotFoundError.description: No such runtime for this team (unknown, malformed, or another team's id — never disclosed which).

RuntimeDestroyedError.description: The runtime is destroyed — terminal. The handle stays readable; nothing else can succeed.

BillingNotReadyError.description: Metered billing catch-up is incomplete. Nothing is provisioned or charged; retry later.

RuntimeNotRunningError.description: No running compute to act on (not provisioned yet, crash-looping, stopped, or destroyed). Unless destroyed, retry after the runtime is observed running.

id.description: Stable key id — the handle for `DELETE /v1/team/keys/{id}`.

prefixHint.description: Display prefix: `plnr_` + the first 4 random characters (e.g. `plnr_ab12`) — enough to recognise a key in a list, never enough to use it.

last4.description: The key’s last 4 characters, to disambiguate keys that share a prefix.

name.description: The optional display name set at mint; null when unnamed.

createdAt.description: When the key was minted (ISO-8601 UTC).

lastUsedAt.description: Approximate time of the key’s most recent authenticated request (best-effort, throttled to ≤ 1 update/minute); null until first used.

expiresAt.description: When the key expires, if an expiry was set at mint; null = never expires (the machine-credential norm). An expired key fails authentication exactly like a revoked one.

revokedAt.description: When the key was revoked; null = active. A revoked key is preserved for audit and fails authentication on its next request.

RuntimeKeyUnavailableError.description: Runtime key rotation requires a non-destroyed runtime created with `spawn: true`.

config.description: Opaque workload config, base64 over the wire. Never parsed. Max 1 MiB encoded. Delivery: the DECODED bytes are mounted read-only at `/etc/planir/config` inside the workload — no env-var channel exists. Handling: held server-side solely for delivery; never parsed, logged, or echoed in error bodies. Replacing config rolls the workload only when the decoded bytes change; a byte-identical replace does not restart it.

PolicyRefusedError.description: A policy gate (not shape validation) refused a well-formed request; the message names the gate.

env.description: Plain environment variables delivered to the workload process. Keys match [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*; the JSON-encoded map is capped at 128 KiB. Replacing env rolls the workload only when the map actually changes; a byte-identical replace does not restart it. Echoed on reads; never logged or echoed in error bodies.

url.description: Opaque, placement-free reach handle (e.g. https://<port>--<id>.<base>). The client parses nothing out of it; the shape is not a wire contract.

port.description: The internal port to resolve. The caller always names it.

metadata.description: Free-form correlation labels. Keys match [A-Za-z0-9._-]+ (max 64 chars), values max 256 chars, at most 32 entries. Echoed on reads; filterable on the list endpoint via `?metadata.<key>=<value>`. Never interpreted by the platform.

cpuSeconds.description: vCPU-seconds over confirmed allocation spans (string — big number).

preservedRootfsByteSeconds.description: Counter, not money: compressed runtime-layer bytes recorded for committed rootfs images integrated over billable presence. Excludes allocated rootfs tiers, shared base-image layers, volume capacity, and storage-system overhead.

ingressBytes.description: Current UTC month interface-level ingress bytes, regardless of the usage query window. Ingress is free and uncapped.

egressBytes.description: Current UTC month measured egress bytes, regardless of the usage query window. This interface-level counter includes everything crossing the runtime workload network interface, including exec/Process traffic, but exec/Process transport is outside the rate cap; image pulls do not cross it. Values trail live traffic by one sampling interval normally and remain stale through a sampling outage until recovery books the full delta. That delta belongs to the later sample month; final churn may under-read, and a UTC boundary can skew by one interval or the recovery delta. Measured for fair-use only and never a billing input.

type.description: Event vocabulary today: `created`, `desired-state-changed`, `config-updated`, `env-updated`, `network-updated`, `restart-requested`, `force-terminate-requested`, `allocated`, `deallocated`, plus one event per observed-phase transition (`provisioning`, `unschedulable`, `running`, `stopping`, `stopped`, `error`, `destroying`, `destroyed`), plus two rootfs-preservation events: `stop-failed` (a stop could not commit the rootfs; it retries while the rootfs is still available) and `rootfs-changes-lost` (the rootfs could not be captured before it was reclaimed — the stop concluded and `start` resumes the newest previously-committed image, without the changes written since it). The set is additive over time — treat unknown types as audit records. Events are the audit/wake-up channel; the authoritative state is always `GET /v1/runtimes/{id}` `observed.phase`.

data.description: Free-form per-type payload. Observed-phase events (including `error`) carry `{generation}` only — no failure diagnosis, by design: events are wake-up signals, not state. The WHY of an `error` phase is read from the runtime itself — `observed.restarts` and `observed.lastExit {reason, exitCode, at}` describe the box agent, while `observed.entrypoint` describes the customer program. `GET /v1/runtimes/{id}/logs` carries the program’s own words.

name.description: The human handle, unique within the team.

sizeBytes.description: Provisioned size in bytes — the hard device-enforced cap. Durability: every live volume is backed up daily to off-site object storage — 7-day retention. Backups are crash-consistent disaster-recovery copies: a restore point is normally under 24 hours old and never silently older than 26 hours — past that the platform raises an alarm. Keep your own backups of critical data. A live volume restore is on request today and arrives as a NEW volume (self-serve restore is planned). Volumes are not live-replicated.

deleteWithRuntime.description: true = a runtime-managed `/data` volume (auto-created at runtime create, deleted with its runtime); false = standalone (runtime destroy detaches it instead — the volume and its data outlive the runtime).

state.description: creating = backing storage is provisioning; available = unattached, attachable via runtime create `volumeId`, deletable; attached = held by a runtime for that runtime's whole LIFE (stop does not release it — only destroy does).

runtimeId.description: The holding runtime. Present exactly while `state` is `attached`.

region.description: The volume's home location, stamped at create and fixed for its life. A runtime created with this `volumeId` is placed here (runtime-follows-volume).

provisionedAt.description: When backing storage provisioning was proven; null while `state` is `creating`.

VolumeNameConflictError.description: A volume with this name already exists in the team — names are unique per team.

name.description: The human handle, unique within the team (duplicate → 409 CONFLICT). Lowercase DNS-label shape: `[a-z0-9]` with interior hyphens, 1–63 chars. Names beginning `data-` are reserved for runtime-managed `/data` volumes (400).

sizeBytes.description: Provisioned size in bytes — a hard cap enforced by the device itself (the workload hits plain ENOSPC at the brim; deleting files frees space immediately). Fixed for the volume's life (no resize in v1). Billed as provisioned byte-seconds from `provisionedAt` to accepted deletion, attached or not. Durability: every live volume is backed up daily to off-site object storage — 7-day retention. Backups are crash-consistent disaster-recovery copies: a restore point is normally under 24 hours old and never silently older than 26 hours — past that the platform raises an alarm. Keep your own backups of critical data. A live volume restore is on request today and arrives as a NEW volume (self-serve restore is planned). Volumes are not live-replicated.

family.description: The preset family whose runtimes will use this volume. Required placement intent: the selected home must offer this family in the requested/default location. Discover families and live availability via GET /v1/regions.

region.description: The location to home the volume in — the same choice runtime create takes. Omitted: the default location. A location that does not offer `family` → 422; one with no capacity right now → 503 (nothing provisioned). See `GET /v1/regions`. The home is fixed for the volume's life: a runtime attaching this volume is placed here (data gravity — the runtime follows the volume, never the reverse).

VolumeNotFoundError.description: No such volume for this team (unknown, malformed, or another team's id — never disclosed which).

VolumeBusyError.description: The volume is attached: attachment spans the holding runtime's whole life — stop does not release it. Destroy the runtime first; no force-detach exists in v1.

host.description: The normalized registry host used for automatic team-scoped matching; `POST /v1/runtimes` needs no credential field.

updatedAt.description: Moves when the stored credential changes. This timestamp does not prove propagation to later pulls.

RegistryHostExistsError.description: The team already holds a credential for this registry host — at most one per host (matching stays deterministic). Rotate or delete the existing credential instead.

host.description: The registry host this credential authenticates, e.g. `ghcr.io`, `docker.io`, `myregistry.example:8443`. Normalized on write (lowercased, scheme stripped, Docker Hub aliases folded to `docker.io`); a path (`ghcr.io/org`) is refused — credentials are host-scoped. At most one credential exists per host. Fresh create uses the current committed credential when it contacts that host's origin. Later origin pulls observe changes only after asynchronous propagation; the prior state can remain effective until then. Rejected effective credentials are not retried anonymously.

username.description: Registry username — provider-specific (`_json_key` for GAR, `org+robot` for quay).

password.description: Registry password / token (write-only — no read ever returns it). Use a scoped, long-lived pull secret: GHCR PAT (`read:packages`), GitLab deploy token, quay robot token, GAR service-account JSON, ACR service-principal password.

RegistryCredentialNotFoundError.description: No such registry credential for this team (unknown, malformed, or another team's id — never disclosed which).

password.description: The replacement password / token (write-only). Running runtimes are untouched. Later origin pulls can use it after asynchronous propagation; the prior state can remain effective until then.

id.description: Preset id — the shape to request: a runtime whose `resources` exactly match a preset's cpu/memory is billed at that preset's rates.

family.description: Display grouping (`co` = Cost Optimized, shared vCPU; `gp` = General Purpose, dedicated vCPU). Grouping only — availability is not decided by family.

cpuMillis.description: Customer workload container CPU quota in millicores (1000 = 1 vCPU of quota).

memoryBytes.description: Customer workload container hard memory limit in bytes.

hourlyMicrocents.description: Metered compute rate per hour, in microcents (1 USD = 100,000,000).

monthlyCeilingMicrocents.description: Per-runtime compute cap per UTC calendar month, in microcents: however long the runtime runs within a month, its compute line never exceeds this.

storageMicrocentsPerGibMonth.description: Volume storage rate per GiB (2^30 bytes) per month, in microcents.

storageFreeBytes.description: Free volume allowance per runtime, in bytes — storage bills only the excess.

region.description: The public location label (e.g. "brq") — a plain string, never an enum; new locations appear additively. The value create requests accept as `region`.

families.description: Per-family availability at this location, family-ASC. A catalogued-but-full family stays LISTED with `available: false`; an EMPTY array means no family is catalogued here at all (the label listed so it is discoverable ahead of commissioning) — two different facts.

family.description: A preset family offered at this location (see GET /v1/presets).

available.description: Whether this location can take the family's smallest preset right now. `false` = full, draining, or not yet commissioned — a create naming this location refuses 503 until it flips. Derived live on every read; re-read rather than remember.

kind.description: root = the platform operator; customer = an ordinary tenant.

200.description: Events after the given cursor, in ascending cursor order. Consistency, honestly stated: cursor values are assigned in insert order, but visibility is transactional — two writers (your own mutations and the platform’s observations) can commit out of order, so an event with a LOWER cursor can become visible momentarily after a higher one has already been served. The skew window is bounded by writer transaction lifetime (milliseconds in practice; single-digit seconds is a safe ceiling). A consumer that persists a resume cursor should therefore re-read a short trailing window and dedupe by cursor — delivery is at-least-once under that discipline, and no event is ever mutated or deleted once visible.

post.description: Starts backing-storage provisioning — a 201 returns the volume in `creating`; it becomes `available` after the backing storage binds. Attach it by creating a runtime with `volumeId` once available. The volume is homed for a required preset `family` at create (optional `region`, the same choice runtime create takes; the response echoes it) and stays there for life — a runtime attaching it is placed there. Billing accrues provisioned byte-seconds from `provisionedAt` to accepted deletion, attached or not — so metered admission gates here exactly as on runtime create: a non-positive balance is a 402. Durability: every live volume is backed up daily to off-site object storage — 7-day retention. Backups are crash-consistent disaster-recovery copies: a restore point is normally under 24 hours old and never silently older than 26 hours — past that the platform raises an alarm. Keep your own backups of critical data. A live volume restore is on request today and arrives as a NEW volume (self-serve restore is planned). Volumes are not live-replicated.
